name: India (CDSCO)
about: The package insert (prescribing information) of a new drug approved by CDSCO, the carton, and the label on the strip or container. Label particulars follow Rule 96 of the Drugs Rules, 1945, schedule warnings follow Rule 97 (as amended in 2018), the QR code follows Schedule H2, and the price display follows the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013. Where a check follows common practice rather than a rule text, its rule card says so.

watch.title: Schedule H2 QR codes for more products
watch.text: The QR code requirement, in force since 1 August 2023 for the top 300 brands, is being extended: vaccines, anti-cancer and NDPS drugs from 1 July 2027 and antimicrobials from 1 July 2028. The app checks a product only when it is marked as in scope.

watch.title: Excipients in QR codes
watch.text: The Health Ministry has said it will amend the Drugs Rules so that QR codes also carry excipient details. Until the amendment is final, the app does not require them.
